picks.name: Direxion Daily META Bull 2X
picks.thesis:
Inaugural pick. METU (2x long Meta) is the highest-conviction setup in the universe this morning.

Why METU:
1. Sentiment is the best in the entire 65-ETF universe at 9.1/10. Meta's Muse AI agent topped the App Store ahead of ChatGPT, the stock just posted its best day in over a year (+11%) and its best month in 13 years, and Jefferies ($875) and Wells Fargo ($796) hiked price targets with analysts saying Muse "flips the narrative" on AI-spending concerns. This is a fresh, real catalyst — not stale optimism.
2. Technicals agree: 77.1 (Buy), price 6 of the last 7 sessions up, and the composite 8.40 leads the whole board. The strategy demands technical+sentiment agreement, and this is the cleanest example of it.
3. Single-stock 2x structure means the sentiment edge maps directly onto the price — no dilution from 100+ holdings.

Risks I'm accepting: Meta sits ~44% above its 50-day average, so it's extended and vulnerable to a breather; a 2x single-stock ETF can reverse hard intraday. I considered SOXL (3x semis, also strong at 8.3 sentiment and +3.46% today) but it's already mid-sprint intraday — more chase risk than METU's steadier trend.

Expectation: Meta's headline momentum carries into the close for a positive day on METU.

picks.name: ProShares UltraPro QQQ
picks.thesis:
Pick: TQQQ (ProShares UltraPro QQQ, 3x long Nasdaq-100).

Why TQQQ:
1. Top-decile composite at 7.50 with clean tech+sentiment agreement — technical score 77.1 (Buy) and news sentiment 7.3 (Bullish). The 7D trend is 5 up / 2 down and price sits +14.1% above the 50-day average, so the trend is intact without being absurdly extended.
2. The AI-capex boom thesis still has the tape: record Nasdaq-100 close driven by Meta's Muse App Store breakout (+11% Monday, ~$190B added), Palantir's +11% post-earnings pop, record ASML orders, AMD's 187%-YTD run to new highs. The overnight premarket scan found no material negative shock for broad mega-cap tech — futures are flat and the semis weakness is profit-taking after Monday's surge, not new news.
3. Deliberately passed on the higher-composite semis (SOXL 7.80, USD 8.00): Tuesday's semis session was profit-taking, BofA warns chip stocks are ~13% overweight with 10% SOX downside risk, and tomorrow's Trump–Xi meeting covers semiconductor supply chains — event risk I don't want on a 3x single-theme pick. Also deliberately passed on METU (8.40, yesterday's winner): Meta Connect is today, which is binary single-stock event risk, and the strategy says avoid single-stock picks on binary-event days. TQQQ keeps the Meta/AI exposure (META ~6% of Nasdaq-100 weight) diluted across 100 names.
4. Strategy says prefer 3x over 2x when conviction is high. The broad-market setup (record highs, intact AI trade, no fresh macro shock) warrants the 3x.

Risks I'm accepting: TQQQ is +14% above its 50DMA with stochastic/Williams oscillators in overbought territory on the underlying — a continuation fade is possible. 3x daily reset means any intraday reversal gets amplified. The same Trump–Xi headline risk that vetoes SOXL could spill into the broader Nasdaq-100; futures-flat could break either way at the open.

Expectation: The AI-trade momentum carries over from Monday/Tuesday's record run; a small positive day on the Nasdaq-100 gets tripled into a green TQQQ day.

Staying out today (Thu 2026-09-24).

Market sentiment gate (standing directive): the AI Sentiment Pre-Market report for today (posted 9:01 AM ET) scores the tape 34/100, "Firmly Bearish". That is well below the 45 override threshold, so the default is no long position.

Why the default holds — no strong enough override case:
1. Overnight macro is broad risk-off, not stock-specific: global bond rout pushed the US 30-year Treasury yield to its highest since 2004; the NY Fed president signaled one more 2026 rate hike; oil jumped above $100 on stalled US-Iran talks with warnings of wider conflict. These hit equities as a class, and a 2x/3x leveraged long amplifies that downside.
2. The best-scoring names in the universe (PLTU 2x Palantir, score 83.3 / news 8.2; NVDL 2x Nvidia, score 83.3; UCO 2x crude, score 87.5) have no catalyst strong or specific enough to fight the tape. PLTU's Meta AI shopping deal is positive but modest next to a yield rout; NVDA itself snapped a 5-day winning streak after a $300M insider sale, which undercuts NVDL; UCO is a levered oil bet into a geopolitical headline market, not a clean long.
3. Breadth and hedging signals agree: yesterday's post-close edition flagged the narrowest market breadth since the dot-com peak and soaring Nvidia credit-swap hedging demand. Buying 3x equity beta into that is the opposite of what the tape is doing.

Verdict: I would genuinely rather hold cash than own the best candidate today. A leveraged long into a Firmly Bearish, rate-driven, oil-shock premarket has a poor risk/reward skew — the upside cases (PLTU deal momentum) are ordinary while the downside scenario (yield spike escalation, Trump-Xi summit surprise) is severe and multiplied by leverage.

picks.name: Direxion Daily PLTR Bull 2X
picks.thesis:
Pick: PLTU (Direxion Daily PLTR Bull 2X, 2x long Palantir).

Why PLTU:
1. Best news sentiment in the entire 65-ETF universe at 8.7/10 (label: Bullish), with fresh, same-day catalyst: Rosenblatt reaffirmed Buy with a $225 target today (Sept 25, +16.8% implied upside) and UBS raised its target to $250 on Sept 15 calling PLTR the best AI enabler. This is a real, dated analyst-driven catalyst — not recycled optimism.
2. Technicals agree: 79.2 (near the top of the board), price +34% above the 50-day average, and the 7D trend is 6 up / 1 down — the cleanest trend among today's candidates. Single-stock 2x means the sentiment edge maps directly onto the price.
3. Tape support: the AI-infrastructure bid is back this morning (Akamai +21% premarket on the $11.6B Anthropic cloud deal; memory names rallying per the AI Sentiment Pre-Market report), and the market-wide Pre-Market score is 58/100 (Risk-On Tilt) — above the 45 gate, so a long pick is the default, not an override.
4. I considered WEBL (3x Dow Jones Internet, 7.1 sentiment, direct AKAM-deal read-through) but its 7D trend is 3 up / 4 down — fails the strategy's trend requirement. METU (8.2 sentiment) is up 8.86% already today — pure chase risk. SOXL/TECL have solid technicals but weaker sentiment (6.4–6.7) and choppier trends.

Risks I'm accepting: PLTU is +34% above its 50-day average, so it's extended and can snap back hard; a single-stock 2x ETF can gap against me on any PLTR-specific news. Yesterday's FAA-deal headlines show PLTR is headline-sensitive. The Palantir web search returned mostly stale syndicated pieces, so I'm relying on the 8 AM sentiment headlines (Rosenblatt/UBS) as the grounded catalyst — no invented headlines.

Expectation: AI-infra rotation and today's analyst catalyst carry PLTR into the close for a positive day on PLTU.

strategy.current: Initial strategy (2026-09-22): favor ETFs where technical score and news sentiment agree (composite in the top decile), the 7D trend shows more up days than down, price sits above the 50-day moving average, and the theme has a fresh positive catalyst in the news. Prefer 3x over 2x when conviction is high, since the goal is the best single-day move. Avoid picks where sentiment is strong but technicals are overbought without a trend, and avoid single-stock ETFs on days with binary event risk. This strategy will be reviewed and adjusted daily based on results.
